sample.n_individuals: 879,647 individuals are given as the analysis sample in footnote 25 (p. 279), against 880,708 observations stated on p. 266

construction_notes: Two-step group-means estimator: each outcome is first regressed on individual-level predetermined controls (gender and month-of-birth indicators; maternal month-of-birth indicators for second-generation outcomes) together with municipality x birth-year fixed effects; the resulting conditional means are then used as dependent variables in municipality x birth-year cell regressions weighted by cell size.

Human capital index: years of schooling, an indicator for more than nine years of compulsory schooling and the log of average wage income over ages 30-60 are each standardized by subtracting the control group mean and dividing by the control group standard deviation, then averaged with equal weights (Kling, Liebman, and Katz 2007). The control group is all municipality x birth-cohort cells without an approved preschool by age 3 among the 138 ever-implementing municipalities.
Wage income is expressed in 2012 terms and averaged over all ages observable between 30 and 60 before taking logs.
Survival analyses left-censor the data at age 50 because the register data start in 1980.

Municipality characteristics exist only for election and census years: vote shares are imputed from the most recent previous election, census variables are linearly interpolated, with interpolated values constrained to the 0-100 range where necessary.
Treatment is based on the year of first government approval of a preschool rather than its establishment; only 62 municipalities have an approval year later than the establishment year.

NHV treatment dates for the 28 sample municipalities without an approved program by 1949 are imputed from Skjernbaek (various years) publication lists (year of the previous publication, or 'never treated').

Preschool enrollment rates are constructed by interpolating the enrolled-children counts from the nine publication years, aggregating to municipality x year, and dividing by the number of survivors past age 1 in urban municipalities for 1939-1950; the paper divides its estimates by about 0.1 to approximate treatment-on-the-treated effects.

claims.statement: Access to a government-approved preschool in the municipality of birth at age 3 raises the adult human capital index of exposed cohorts (specification with municipality and cohort fixed effects and municipality time-varying controls, without county trends).

definition.value: An indicator equal to one for cohorts that had at least one government-approved preschool in their municipality of birth at age 3, and zero otherwise. Treatment is assigned from the municipality of birth (merged from the parish of birth) and the year of first government approval of a preschool, taken from nine preschool directories covering 1921-1960; approval rather than establishment is used so that the treatment is access to a regulated, high-quality preschool.

timing.value: measured at age 3, i.e. in the calendar year the birth cohort turns 3 (birth cohorts 1930-1957, preschool approvals 1933-1960)

definition.value: Equally weighted average of three standardized human capital measures - years of schooling at age 50, an indicator for having more than nine years of compulsory schooling at age 50, and the natural log of average wage income (in 2012 terms) over all ages observable between 30 and 60 - each standardized by subtracting the control group mean and dividing by the control group standard deviation, as in Kling, Liebman, and Katz (2007). The control group is all municipality x birth-cohort cells without an approved preschool by age 3 among the 138 ever-implementing municipalities. The regression dependent variable is the municipality x birth-year conditional mean from a first-step individual-level regression on gender and month-of-birth indicators.

evidence.how: Searched the data section (pp. 262-266) and the table notes: the paper names its individual-level source only as 'administrative population register data for the years 1980-2012' and never gives a Danish register code or variable name (no BEF/IND/UDDA codes, no PERINDKIALT-style variable names).

Table 4 prints the coefficient and, in brackets, the municipality-clustered standard error; it prints no p-value, no confidence interval and no standard deviation of the outcome, and no control mean for this outcome.

Preschool access is measured at age 3 and the index combines measures taken at age 50 and wage income averaged over ages 30-60; expressed as years since exposure this is 27 to 57 years after treatment (50-3 = 47 for the schooling components).

links.pointer_quote: We document a 0.024 standard deviation (SD) increase in a summary human capital index, driven by a 0.1 year rise in the average number of years of schooling, a 1.7 percentage point increase in the likelihood of obtaining more than a compulsory education, and a 1.7 percent higher average wage income over the ages of 30 to 60.

claims.statement: Access to a government-approved preschool at age 3 raises the probability of having more than compulsory education at age 50 by 1.7 percentage points (preferred specification).

definition.value: An indicator equal to one for cohorts that had at least one government-approved preschool in their municipality of birth at age 3, and zero otherwise. Treatment is assigned from the municipality of birth (merged from the parish of birth) and the year of first government approval of a preschool, taken from nine preschool directories covering 1921-1960; approval rather than establishment is used so that the treatment is access to a regulated, high-quality preschool.

timing.value: measured at age 3, i.e. in the calendar year the birth cohort turns 3 (birth cohorts 1930-1957, preschool approvals 1933-1960)

definition.value: An indicator for having more than nine years of compulsory schooling, measured at age 50. The regression dependent variable is the municipality x birth-year conditional mean from a first-step individual-level regression on gender and month-of-birth indicators.

timing.value: measured at age 50 in the 1980-2012 register data

units.value: share of the cohort (indicator); a coefficient of 0.017 is 1.7 percentage points

magnitude.interpretation: 1.7 percentage points (3 percent at the control mean) more likely to have completed more than compulsory education; an approximate TOT effect of 17 percentage points

estimand.target_population: cohorts born 1930-1957 in the 138 municipalities that ever had a government-approved preschool by 1960; intent-to-treat with respect to access, since preschool attendance is not observed (the paper divides its estimates by an approximate enrollment rate of 0.1 to obtain treatment-on-the-treated magnitudes)

claims.statement: For cohorts without access to an approved preschool at age 3, access to the Nurse Home Visiting program at birth raises the likelihood of survival beyond age 65 by 0.5 percentage points.

definition.value: An indicator equal to one for cohorts that had the Nurse Home Visiting program in their municipality in their year of birth and zero otherwise. NHV approval dates 1937-1949 come from Danish National Board of Health records in the Danish National Archives; for the 28 sample municipalities without an approved program by 1949 a less precise date is imputed from Skjernbaek (various years) lists. Once established, NHV assigned trained-nurse visits to all newborns and their mothers about ten times in the first year of life.

timing.value: measured in the year of birth (birth cohorts 1930-1957)

definition.value: An indicator for surviving beyond age 65. The survival data are left-censored so that all individuals in the analysis sample enter the risk period at age 50 (the register data start in 1980, so the oldest cohorts must have survived to age 50 to be observed). definition.value: Indicators for the (first-generation) cohorts' age in the year of the first preschool approval in their municipality of birth, from -2 to 11, grouped into two-year bins, with ages 6-7 as the omitted category, plus indicators for being born more than two years after approval and for being older than 11 at approval. The claim refers to the bins covering cohorts aged 3 years or less at approval (-2&-1, 0&1, 2&3), i.e. the cohorts with full potential preschool exposure.

definition.value: Equally weighted average of three standardized human capital measures - years of schooling at age 50, an indicator for having more than nine years of compulsory schooling at age 50, and the natural log of average wage income (in 2012 terms) over all ages observable between 30 and 60 - each standardized by subtracting the control group mean and dividing by the control group standard deviation, as in Kling, Liebman, and Katz (2007). The control group is all municipality x birth-cohort cells without an approved preschool by age 3 among the 138 ever-implementing municipalities. The regression dependent variable is the municipality x birth-year conditional mean from a first-step individual-level regression on gender and month-of-birth indicators.

claims.statement: Access to the Nurse Home Visiting program at birth reduces the likelihood of being diagnosed with cardiovascular disease.

definition.value: An indicator equal to one for cohorts that had the Nurse Home Visiting program in their municipality in their year of birth and zero otherwise.
